mage.protectedInterfaceOriginal: A Nuke Chain requires different named spells of the chosen element; completing a three-spell chain vents 2 Dissonance. Repeating one nuke builds Refrain normally.
engine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Intelligence is the Mage class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Mage levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Intelligence modifier) unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Mage spell attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier. Mage spell save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier.

Spellcasting and Resonance Pool are automatic class features, never selection taxes. Use the Mage maximum Resonance Point pool and ordinary spell-rank costs from authoritative Core Systems Known Descent V 2. All Mage card RP costs and ordinary spell RP costs come from that same pool. There are no spell slots. A long rest restores RP according to Core V 2; other existing recovery rules remain separate unless this pilot explicitly overrides them.

Named Mage cards tagged mage-spell, and the three Focus finishers are spells for Focus, Nuke Chain, Refrain, concentration, Counterspell and other spell-referencing mechanics. Their printed RP cost replaces an ordinary rank cost; do not charge both. Generic Overcast is disabled for these class-card spells during this pilot unless a card expressly enables it. They receive no extra class-level Burn or Dissonance simply for being card spells; ordinary Core V 2 spell-risk rules still apply where applicable.

Elemental Focus is gained automatically at Mage level 2. Choose Fire, Cold or Lightning and automatically gain the corresponding Focus card. Your selected Focus determines the element used by Elemental Bolt, Elemental Surge, your Focus finisher and other effects that refer to your chosen element. Unless Elemental Pivot or another explicit effect changes it, the choice is permanent in this draft.

NUKE CHAIN. Track your last three consecutive Focus-eligible spell casts. A Focus-eligible cast is a Mage or ordinary spell that deals your currently chosen Fire, Cold or Lightning damage type and is identified by a distinct spell or card name. A spell of another element or a non-elemental spell clears the chain. The last three eligible casts must have three different names. Repeating one chosen-element spell remains a legal cast but shifts the three-cast window and follows ordinary Refrain rules; repetition does not receive special protection from Dissonance.

When the third different named chosen-element spell in the current three-cast window resolves, complete the Nuke Chain, reduce Dissonance by 2 to a minimum of 0, and prime your selected Focus finisher until the end of your next regular Mage turn. Chain completion occurs whether targets hit or save, provided all three spells were legally cast and resolved. A finisher is not itself a chain-building spell. Using the finisher or allowing it to expire clears the chain and the primed state.

FOCUS FINISHERS. A primed Focus finisher is a Bonus Action Mage spell costing 2 RP and is usable once per completed Nuke Chain. Each finisher also has a 3-round recharge. A completed chain can prime a finisher whose recharge is still positive, but the primed use expires normally if the recharge does not become ready in time. Finisher recharge is subject to the universal positive-counter reset limit of once per ability per round.

RESONANCE SURGE. Once per short rest, when you begin casting a damaging Mage spell, you may spend 2 additional RP after validating the spell's normal cost. Add S d8 damage of one damage type already dealt by that spell to one of its damage rolls. Resonance Surge does not count as Overcast, does not independently alter Dissonance or Burn, does not create another spell cast, and does not advance the Nuke Chain separately.

Only one concentration effect may be maintained at a time. Starting another concentration effect ends the first. Damage prompts the current Core Systems concentration save; for this pilot any required half-damage rounding is down. Round recharge counters tick once at the start of your regular initiative turn even if incapacitated, and every uninterrupted 6 seconds outside initiative. Only positive counters may be shortened or reset and each named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant additional Actions, Bonus Actions or Reactions. Mage summons and companions do not receive independent damaging turns: all Mage-controlled conjured companions share one Companion Command per Mage regular turn. Spend one Bonus Action to command exactly one companion to move up to its Speed and use one damaging or control action from its stat block. Uncommanded companions may move to remain near you and take Dodge but cannot deal damage or impose control.

ELEMENTAL FAMILIAR. Conjure Elemental Familiar creates one familiar matching your current Focus; you may have only one elemental familiar. AC = 12 + PB; HP = 5 + Mage level + M; Speed 30 feet; Lightning familiar additionally has Fly 30 feet, Fire has resistance to fire, Cold has resistance to cold. It uses your saves and PB where required. Elemental Dart: ranged spell attack using your Mage spell attack, range 30 feet, hit S d4 damage of its element. It cannot generate RP, Dissonance, Focus casts, corpses, XP, loot or kill-trigger resources.

LICH COMPANION SYSTEM. A successful Lich transformation unlocks three unique bound elite companions: Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound. You can maintain at most one of each, maximum three total. They return at full HP after a completed long rest unless a campaign consequence expressly prevents it. A destroyed elite leaves no usable corpse and cannot generate XP, loot, RP, Nuke Chain credit, Soul Reservoir or kill-based resources. Soulbound Ritual can return one before a long rest.

BONEFLAYER. Medium undead; AC 14; HP = 12 + 2 × Mage level; Speed 30 feet. Bone Shards: range 60 feet, your Mage spell attack, hit 2d6 + S necrotic. Fear Pulse: instead of Bone Shards, enemies of your choice within 10 feet make Wisdom saves against your Mage DC; failure causes Frightened until the end of their next turn; recharge 3 rounds. Grave Miasma: instead of Bone Shards, one 10-foot-radius point within 30 feet persists until the start of your next turn; enemies entering or starting there take 1d6 necrotic once; recharge 3 rounds.

DREADBLADE. Medium undead; AC 16; HP = 16 + 3 × Mage level; Speed 30 feet. Disrupting Blade: melee spell attack using your Mage attack bonus, reach 5 feet, hit 1d8 + S necrotic. If the target is concentrating it immediately makes its concentration save with disadvantage. On a natural 20, the target is Weakened until the end of its next turn, taking -1 to attack rolls. Dreadblade has advantage on saves against forced movement.

WRAITHBOUND. Medium undead; AC 14; HP = 10 + 2 × Mage level; Fly 40 feet and can hover. While it has not attacked or imposed control since the end of its previous turn, it is Invisible; attacking ends that state until the end of its next turn. Wraith Strike: melee spell attack using your Mage attack bonus, reach 5 feet, hit 1d8 + S necrotic. On a natural 20, the target makes a Constitution save against your Mage DC; failure Stuns it until the end of its next turn.

LICH TRANSFORMATION READINESS. At Mage level 10 a character may select Lich only after obtaining either one Soul Coin or two ritual participants, binding at least two named mini-bosses as guardians, securing a planar nexus and surviving the Director's divine-echo encounter. A third bound guardian grants +2 to the final ritual check. If both ritual participants are willing, the final ritual check has advantage.

Before the irreversible Lich roll, the Director must explicitly tell the player the historical failure stakes: permanent loss of spellcasting, transformation into a cursed melee undead NPC, hostile faction consequences, cursed-gear restriction and no further XP as that retired PC. The player must explicitly opt into that retirement risk before rolling. If the player declines, the ritual stops before the roll and the character must choose another Hero path for this playtest; no irreversible consequence is applied.

LICH RITUAL CHECK. After all readiness gates and the divine-echo encounter are completed, roll d20 + Intelligence modifier + Constitution modifier against DC 20, applying the third-guardian +2 and willing-participant advantage where applicable. Success completes the Lich transformation and unlocks its cards and elite companions. Failure after explicit consent applies the historical failure state and the Director pauses for the agreed player-to-NPC handoff before continuing play. No silent PC deletion is permitted.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Mage 1 automatically gains Spellcasting, Resonance Pool and Resonance Surge, then chooses 4 eligible selectable Base cards, at least 2 Active. Mage 2 automatically chooses and gains one Elemental Focus card, then chooses 2 additional Base cards. Mage 3 enters Arcanist and chooses 2 Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Levels 4 through 9 each grant one eligible unselected Base or Arch card; level 9 is an ordinary choice because the historical source has no Arch capstone.

At Mage 10 choose Archmage, Elementalist or, if its ritual succeeds, Lich; choose 2 cards from that Hero path. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base or Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. Mage 20 grants one additional Hero-path choice plus the NEW playtest level-20 class capstone in extra Cards. No historical Hero Finale is implied. ASI/feat milestones remain separate.

All acquisition gates use Mage class level, not total character level. Proficiency bonus remains the normal total-character proficiency bonus. Non-Mage levels do not unlock Elemental Focus, Arcanist, Hero cards, Nuke Chain upgrades, Lich ritual access or the level-20 Mage capstone.

Class-spell ranks are printed in the normalized card data: use the legal maximum Mage rank at that card's minimum class level, capped 9; the three Focus finishers are rank 1. Rank determines Dissonance, Counterspell and rank-limited interactions, not a second RP cost. A shared spell uses the ally's normal Action and caster-side Dissonance at the moment it is cast; it never builds the Mage's Nuke Chain remotely. Spellcasting through Fracture as Lich uses the shared direct-trauma rule.
workedExample: Mage 5 Fire example: Intelligence 16 gives M=3, PB=3 and S=2. For arithmetic illustration, assume the current Core V 2 character sheet gives this Mage 14 RP. Dissonance begins at 4, Fire Focus is selected, the Nuke Chain is empty and all targets are legal.

Turn 1: Elemental Bolt costs 1 RP, so RP 14→13. It is named Elemental Bolt and deals Fire because Fire is the current Focus, so the chain is [Elemental Bolt]. Its attack hits for 2d8+3 fire; Fire Focus adds its printed Burn rider.

Turn 2: the Mage casts a distinct ordinary Fire spell whose Core V 2 cost is 2 RP, so RP 13→11. Because it is a different named Fire spell, the chain becomes [Elemental Bolt, ordinary Fire spell]. Ordinary Core V 2 Refrain/Dissonance rules still apply to that spell independently.

Turn 3: Elemental Surge costs 3 RP, so RP 11→8. It is a third different named Fire spell, completing the exact three-spell Nuke Chain. After it resolves, Dissonance vents 4→2 and Inferno Lance becomes primed through the end of the Mage's next regular turn.

Turn 3 Bonus Action: Inferno Lance is ready and costs 2 RP, so RP 8→6. The Mage fires its 20-foot line. Inferno Lance is a finisher, not another chain-building spell; after it resolves the chain and primed state clear and Inferno Lance receives its printed 3-round recharge.

Turn 4: the Mage uses Resonance Surge with Arcane Barrage. Arcane Barrage costs 3 RP plus 2 additional RP for Surge, so RP 6→1. Surge adds S d8 = 2d8 force damage to one Barrage damage roll. Because Arcane Barrage is non-elemental, it clears any partial Fire chain and Resonance Surge itself does not count as another spell.
balanceQuestions: Does requiring three different named Focus spells make Nuke Chains achievable at the intended cadence without forcing every Mage into the same ordinary-spell repertoire, and are the 2 RP Bonus Action finishers appropriately rewarding for the setup?

Do Resonance Surge, Spell Efficiency, Primal Channeling, Soul Reservoir and Resonance to Flesh keep the shared Core V2 RP economy bounded across multiple encounters rather than creating a sustainable positive-RP loop?

With the one-shared-damaging-command rule, do the elemental familiar and Lich's three elite companions provide meaningful identity without overwhelming the Mage's own Action economy or creating corpse, kill, control or resource farms?

cards.name: Spellcasting

cards.name: Elemental Bolt

cards.name: Elemental Fusion
cards.effect: Elemental Fusion. Tags: mage-spell, elementalist, elemental, damage. Choose your current Focus and one other element among Fire, Cold and Lightning. Make a Mage spell attack. On hit deal S d8 of each chosen element. Pair rider: Fire+Cold reduces Speed by 10 feet and applies 1d4 fire at start of target's next turn; Fire+Lightning removes Reaction until start of target's next turn; Cold+Lightning reduces Speed by 10 feet and prevents opportunity attacks until end of target's next turn. For Nuke Chain purposes this spell counts only as your current Focus element.

source.originalText: Elemental Fusion: Combine two elements to create a hybrid spell with unique effects.

cards.name: Cascade Storm
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to three different creatures within 60 feet
cards.effect: Cascade Storm. Tags: mage-spell, elementalist, fire, cold, lightning, damage. Choose up to three creatures. Resolve one separate Mage spell attack against each: first hit deals S d6 fire and 1d4 fire next turn; second hit deals S d6 cold and Speed -10 feet until end next turn; third hit deals S d6 lightning and removes Reaction until start next turn. If fewer than three targets are chosen, unused elements are lost. For Nuke Chain purposes choose one of the three elements before casting; Cascade Storm counts only as that element.

source.originalText: Cascade Storm: Trigger a sequence of elemental effects that build upon each other.

cards.name: Elemental Absorption
cards.duration: Until end of your next regular turn
cards.effect: Elemental Absorption. Tags: mage-spell, elementalist, protection. Trigger when you would take fire, cold or lightning damage. Gain resistance to that triggering damage type for the triggering event and until the end of your next regular turn. Your next damaging Mage spell before then adds 1d8 of the absorbed type to one damage roll; the bonus is lost after use or expiry. This Reaction spell clears an incompatible current Nuke Chain unless the absorbed type is your current Focus.

source.originalText: Elemental Absorption: Temporarily absorb incoming elemental damage to enhance your next spell.

cards.name: Primal Channeling
cards.effect: Primal Channeling. Tags: elementalist, resonance. During a real encounter, draw ambient elemental energy and restore 2 RP, never above your maximum. You cannot use Primal Channeling outside a real encounter, during a rest, through a summoned proxy or more than once per short rest. It does not count as a spell cast, does not advance Nuke Chain and does not alter Dissonance.

source.originalText: Primal Channeling: Draw raw elemental energy from the environment to empower your spells.

cards.name: Elemental Mastery
cards.effect: Elemental Mastery. Tags: elementalist, focus, mastery. For 3 rounds, Fire, Cold and Lightning Mage spells all count as matching your current Focus for Nuke Chain eligibility. After you complete one three-distinct-name chain during this duration, you may choose any one of the three Focus finishers when it becomes primed, regardless of your current Focus. Only one finisher may be generated by this use. After that finisher resolves or expires, the mastery continues defensively but cannot prime another off-focus finisher.

source.originalText: Elemental Mastery: Temporarily gain mastery over all elements, allowing you to use any elemental finisher regardless of your focus.

cards.name: Undying Spellform
cards.duration: Until end of your next regular turn
cards.effect: Undying Spellform. Tags: lich, undead, death. When damage reduces you to 0 HP without killing you outright, remain conscious and able to take Actions until the end of your next regular turn. You remain at 0 HP, cannot benefit from voluntary movement faster than half Speed, and still suffer ordinary consequences of further damage. If still at 0 HP when the effect ends, become unconscious and suffer one failed death save. Healing above 0 ends this feature early.

source.originalText: Undying Spellform: When reduced to 0 HP, continue casting for 1 full round before death.

cards.name: Soul Reservoir
cards.frequency: At most once per turn and at most S times per encounter
cards.effect: Soul Reservoir. Tags: lich, resonance, damage-over-time. During a real encounter, when a hostile creature takes damage from a damage-over-time effect created by one of your Mage spells, restore 1 RP, never above maximum. The same damage event cannot restore more than 1 RP. Damage to allies, summons, trivial creatures or your own companions does not qualify.

source.originalText: Soul Reservoir: All DoT damage you deal feeds Resonance recovery.

cards.name: Necromantic Mastery
cards.effect: Necromantic Mastery. Tags: lich, necromancy. Once on each of your turns when a Mage spell deals necrotic damage, add S necrotic damage to one damaged target. Your necrotic Mage spells also ignore resistance to necrotic damage; immunity remains immunity. This feature does not convert another spell's damage type and cannot apply to companion attacks unless a card explicitly identifies them as your spell.

source.originalText: Necromantic Mastery: Gain access to enhanced necromancy spells and abilities.

cards.name: Undead Immunities
cards.effect: Undead Immunities. Tags: lich, undead. You are immune to poison damage, the Poisoned condition, disease, Frightened, Charmed and magical sleep. You no longer need to breathe. You still require the normal rest schedule for mechanical recovery and can still be affected by abilities that specifically target undead unless another feature says otherwise.

source.originalText: Undead Immunities: Become immune to poison, disease, fear, sleep, and mind control.

cards.name: Lingering Malice
cards.effect: Lingering Malice. Tags: mage-spell, lich, necrotic, zone, concentration. Choose Fear or Drain when cast. On start and each paid Bonus Action maintenance pulse, enemies in the zone make Wisdom saves. Failure takes S d6 necrotic. Fear mode also Frightens until the start of your next turn. Drain mode lets you gain temporary HP equal to M once per pulse if at least one enemy fails. Maximum 3 pulses; each pulse grants a new save.

source.originalText: Lingering Malice: Create a necrotic zone for 3 rounds that applies Fear or Drain effects.

cards.name: Resonance to Flesh
cards.effect: Resonance to Flesh. Tags: lich, resonance, blood. Choose one direction. RP to Flesh: spend 1-5 RP and regain 2 HP per RP spent. Flesh to RP: lose 2-10 HP in even increments and restore 1 RP per 2 HP lost. HP loss cannot be reduced, redirected or transferred and cannot reduce you below 1 HP. RP cannot exceed maximum. This feature cannot be repeated through Echoes or companions.

source.originalText: Resonance to Flesh: Convert Resonance into HP (or vice versa) once per rest.

cards.name: Flesh to Ash
cards.rangeAndTarget: 15-foot-radius sphere centered at a point within 60 feet
cards.effect: Flesh to Ash. Tags: mage-spell, lich, necrotic, damage. Creatures of your choice in the area make Constitution saves. A target at half maximum HP or more takes S d8 necrotic on failure, half on success. A target below half maximum HP instead takes 2 S d8 necrotic on failure, half on success. Determine the threshold before rolling damage.

source.originalText: Flesh to Ash: Create an AoE burst that doubles damage if target is below 50% HP.

cards.name: Corpse Gateway
cards.rangeAndTarget: One visible corpse within 60 feet and one unoccupied space within 5 feet of it
cards.effect: Corpse Gateway. Tags: mage-spell, lich, teleportation, corpse. Teleport to the chosen unoccupied space adjacent to a visible corpse. The corpse is not consumed or altered. Summoned-companion remains, repeated fragments of the same destroyed creature and illusory corpses are not legal anchors. This non-elemental spell clears an active Nuke Chain.

source.originalText: Corpse Gateway: Teleport to a corpse within line of sight.

cards.name: Soulbound Ritual
cards.rangeAndTarget: One of your destroyed bound elite undead companions within 30 feet or its inert binding token
cards.effect: Soulbound Ritual. Tags: mage-spell, lich, companion, resurrection. Return one destroyed Boneflayer, Dreadblade or Wraithbound to an unoccupied space within 30 feet at half its maximum HP. It gains S+M temporary HP for 1 minute. The returned companion remains subject to the shared Companion Command limit and cannot create a corpse, XP, loot or resource event if destroyed again.

source.originalText: Soulbound Ritual: Revive a fallen undead pet with bonus stats.

cards.name: Resonance Apex — NEW Playtest Capstone
cards.rangeAndTarget: One Mage spell you are beginning to cast
cards.effect: Before paying for one Mage spell, reduce that spell's printed RP cost by up to 10 RP, minimum final cost 0. This capstone is new playtest design and is not claimed as a recovered historical feature. The cast cannot also use Resonance Surge or generic Overcast. It remains one spell cast, follows ordinary Focus/Nuke Chain rules, and alters Dissonance only through rules that would already apply to that cast.

mage.authoringNotes: Provisional; editorial review applied; human table balance testing required

dragoon.protectedInterfaceOriginal: If the Dragoon moved at least 20 feet before a Weave cast, reduce that cast's Dissonance gain by 1 (minimum 0); Momentum carries the note through motion.
dragoon.rpAuthority: Explicit fallback: Cleric CoreV2 curve ×0.35, halves upward
engine: Strength is the class ability. Momentum starts/ends encounters at 0; cap 5, rising to 7 with Momentum Overflow or automatically at class 9. On each regular turn, moving at least 15 ft under your own power grants 1 Momentum, and damaging an enemy with a weapon attack grants 1 more. These are the only default gains; all gains/refunds together cap 2 per round. Forced movement, teleportation, movement in place, allies and summons cannot farm Momentum. Movement counts actual path traveled toward a tactical destination; one threshold per turn.

A leap technique moves you through an unobstructed arc to a visible unoccupied landing space within its range, adjacent to its target when attacking. Land during the same activation. It spends movement equal to horizontal distance, unless the card expressly supplies additional movement. A leap never gives flight, indefinite airborne immunity or free attacks. You cannot leap through ceilings/walls; vertical height is at most half the printed horizontal range. Safe technique landings do not cause self-fall damage; interrupted/falling travel follows ordinary falling rules. No bonus damage is earned by repeatedly dropping from a ledge.

All attack cards use a wielded polearm unless they explicitly describe a non-weapon save effect. A technique is its own Action, not an Attack Action plus free technique. At class 5 your ordinary Attack Action makes two attacks, at most two even when multiclass features overlap; each technique still gives only printed attacks. This automatic Extra Attack is a new explicit advancement specification for the pilot.

Armor bypass means the exact printed attack bonus or resistance exception, never subtracting a percentage of the target's whole AC. Critical ranges do not stack. A Dragoon can use only one free/Bonus Action leap granted by class features per round; it cannot trigger another free leap. Extra full Actions share the suite-wide cap. Reaction intercepts require a legal path and destination and do not rewind resolved damage.

Spending Momentum pays before resolution; a hit refund cannot pay its own activation. Burn means 1d4 fire at start of target's next 2 turns, nonstacking. Bleed means 1d4 physical at start of next 2 turns; an Action with a healer's kit ends it. Do Ts give no Momentum or critical triggers. Hard denial uses the shared once-per-target/encounter guard.

When casting an ordinary spell after moving at least 20 ft this turn, reduce that cast's Dissonance gain by 1, minimum 0; no automatic RP discount. Dragoon techniques are martial unless their card specifies elemental magic. Use Core V 2 RP and the Dragoon rank gates for separate spellcasting.

Use scheduled Base/Arch/Hero choices. Skybound Assault, Momentum Engine and related passives improve the automatic engine rather than unlock basic movement or generation. Lancer's Apex is automatic 9; at 10 choose Dragon Guardian, Drake Rider or Dragon Tyrant. The corresponding Final Flight is automatic 20. Apex Assault is an active technique despite its source passive heading.
workedExample: Dragoon 5, STR 16, PB 3, S 2, M 3; start Momentum 0. Know Dragon Leap, Momentum Surge, Wyvern's Guard and Draconic Roar at 1; Momentum Engine and Draconic Discipline at 2; Dragonflight and Momentum Overflow at 3. Capacity 7.
Turn 1: Dragon Leap spends 0 Momentum and moves 20 ft of Speed 30. Weapon attack hits: movement+hit each gain 1, ending 2. It rolls weapon damage+2d6. Land immediately.

Turn 2: Bonus Action Momentum Surge spends 2, balance 0, increases movement. Move 20 ft and use ordinary Attack Action: first successful hit and movement return 2 total, even if both attacks hit. End 2.
Turn 3: Dragonflight costs 2, balance 0. It supplies movement up to 60 ft as part of the Action; hit and movement regain 2 within the common cap. End 2; no additional normal Attack Action.
Turn 4: if knocked prone, use Aerial Recovery only if known and your Reaction is available. Its 1 Momentum still counts toward the round gain cap. A second refund cannot exceed 2 total gains.
End encounter: Momentum 0. RP, per-rest uses and other party resources do not refill.
balanceQuestions: Does Momentum stay available without trivial back-and-forth movement?
Do Guardian intercepts compete fairly for Reactions?
Are Tyrant area attacks and Rider extra Actions bounded at high level?

cards.name: Skybound Assault
cards.rangeAndTarget: One target hit by your leap
cards.effect: After a leap moves at least 15 ft and its attack hits, add S damage. Its hit grants ordinary Momentum, not an extra point. This benefit cannot trigger from forced movement or a leap granted by this same feature.

source.originalText: Skybound Assault: Leap to a target and deal +25% damage. Grants 1 Momentum.

cards.name: Draconic Discipline
cards.effect: Gain advantage on saves against being knocked Prone or forcibly moved. It does not protect against Stunned, spell damage or grappling unless the save also imposes one of those named effects.

source.originalText: Draconic Discipline: Gain +10% resistance to knockback and crowd control.

cards.name: Momentum Engine
cards.effect: After your first 15 ft of voluntary movement generates Momentum, ignore the next 5 ft of nonmagical difficult terrain this turn. The movement threshold itself is automatic class engine; this feature does not create another gain trigger.

source.originalText: Momentum Engine: Movement of 3+ tiles in a turn grants 1 Momentum (Max 5).

cards.name: Dragoon's Reach
cards.effect: Increase your wielded polearm's reach by 5 ft, maximum 15 ft. Once/own turn a natural 19 polearm attack that hits critically hits. It does not extend the range of other abilities or stack with another critical-range expansion.

source.originalText: Dragoon's Reach: Polearm attacks strike 1 tile further and have +5% crit chance.

cards.name: Aerial Poise
cards.effect: When a ranged attack hits you during your leap movement, halve its damage. You must spend the Reaction before damage resolves. Remaining airborne between turns cannot be declared to keep this protection active.

source.originalText: Aerial Poise: While airborne, take 25% reduced damage from ranged attacks.

cards.name: Dragon Leap
cards.rangeAndTarget: One polearm enemy at landing point within 30 ft
cards.effect: Leap, spending normal movement, then make one polearm attack. On hit add S d6 weapon-type damage. Legal movement and a hit may each grant 1 Momentum under the common cap. Land immediately; height never adds unbounded damage.

source.originalText: Dragon Leap: Launch yourself into the air and come crashing down on a target up to 30 feet away, dealing damage based on your Strength and height.

cards.name: Piercing Thrust
cards.effect: Make one polearm attack with+2 to the attack roll. On hit add S d4 weapon damage. This is the complete armor-piercing benefit; no percentage of AC is removed and critical range is unchanged.

source.originalText: Piercing Thrust: A powerful spear attack that partially ignores enemy armor and has increased critical hit chance.

cards.name: Wyvern's Guard
cards.effect: The next attack that damages you has damage reduced by S d6+M, minimum 0; then the guard ends. Roll the reduction only when damage occurs. This reduction cannot heal or reflect damage.

source.originalText: Wyvern's Guard: Enter a defensive stance that increases your resistance to damage from the next attack.

cards.name: Momentum Surge
cards.effect: Gain+15 ft Speed and+1 on your next polearm attack this turn. Spend before moving; movement may then generate normal Momentum. Grants no attack, extra Action, Bonus Action or Reaction.

source.originalText: Momentum Surge: Consume 2 Momentum to gain a burst of speed and +1 to your next attack roll.

cards.name: Draconic Roar
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to 3 enemies and 3 allies within 15 ft that hear you
cards.effect: Enemies make WIS saves; failure Frightened of you. Chosen allies gain advantage on their next save against Frightened before duration ends. A creature may repeat the WIS save at its turn end, ending fear on success.

source.originalText: Draconic Roar: Release a intimidating battle cry that can frighten weaker enemies and rally allies.

cards.name: Crater Strike
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to 2 enemies within 5 ft of your leap landing
cards.effect: After your leap attack hits, optionally pay 1; each selected adjacent enemy makes STR save or falls Prone. No additional weapon damage or Momentum gain. Landing on an occupied space is not permitted.

source.originalText: Crater Strike: Leap attack that applies knockdown in a small AoE.

cards.name: Momentum Overflow
cards.effect: Momentum cap becomes 7 early; cap becomes 7 for all Dragoons at 9. When starting a weapon technique with 6 or 7 Momentum, its first hit adds 1d6 damage before costs are deducted. Once/own turn, not per point above 5; no stored overflow beyond 7.

source.originalText: Momentum Overflow: Exceed Momentum cap (Max 7), bonus damage scales with overflow.

cards.name: Piercing Howl
cards.effect: Your next polearm attack gains+2 to hit and ignores resistance to its weapon damage type. Immunity remains. It does not ignore shields, natural armor, cover or arbitrary halves of AC.

source.originalText: Piercing Howl: Next polearm strike ignores 50% armor.

cards.name: Lance Tempo
cards.effect: After moving 15 ft voluntarily, gain+1 AC. If you critically hit with a polearm that turn, add 1d6 weapon damage once. The added die does not double itself or create further critical triggers.

source.originalText: Lance Tempo: If you moved this turn, gain +10% evasion and +10% crit damage.

cards.name: Wyvern's Flow
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self after a damaging leap hit
cards.effect: Regain 1 Momentum within the total 2-per-round gain cap, and shorten one OTHER positive leap cooldown by 1. Shortening uses that ability's reset allowance. No free leap or Action follows.

source.originalText: Wyvern's Flow: Successful leaps refund 1 Momentum and reduce next cooldown by 1.

cards.name: Apex Assault
cards.rangeAndTarget: One enemy in polearm reach after leap up to 30 ft
cards.effect: Spend K Momentum and leap using normal movement. Make one polearm attack; on hit add min(K, 5)d6 weapon damage. On a miss no bonus damage; expenditure remains. Gains from this activation cannot exceed the common cap.

source.originalText: Apex Assault: Ultimate leap: high damage finisher that consumes all Momentum.

cards.name: Lancer's Apex
cards.cost: All Momentum at current maximum; 1 short-rest use
cards.effect: Before paying the leap's Momentum cost, spend all maximum Momentum instead and use that leap as a Bonus Action, still paying other costs. It cannot trigger another free leap. Damage and hit generation use ordinary caps; this grants no extra Bonus Action.

source.originalText: Capstone – Lancer's Apex: Leap attacks now cost no action if performed at max Momentum (1/encounter).

cards.name: Dragonflight
cards.rangeAndTarget: One enemy adjacent to landing within 60 ft
cards.effect: Leap up to 60 ft as additional movement supplied by this Action. Make one polearm attack on landing; on hit add(S+1)d6 weapon damage. No damage scaling from distance/height and no remaining flight.

source.originalText: Dragonflight: An enhanced leap ability that allows you to jump twice as high and far, with increased damage based on distance traveled.

cards.name: Spear Cyclone
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to 3 distinct enemies in polearm reach
cards.effect: Make one polearm attack against each. No target is attacked twice. Hit-based Momentum can be gained only once this turn regardless of number of hits; movement and refund caps still apply.

source.originalText: Spear Cyclone: Spin your polearm in a wide arc, striking all enemies within range and building Momentum for each hit.

cards.name: Momentum Burst
cards.effect: Spend K Momentum. Next polearm hit this turn adds min(K, 4)d6 weapon damage. If the next attack misses the effect ends. It does not widen critical range or multiply another added damage package.

source.originalText: Momentum Burst: Consume all Momentum to gain a significant boost to your next attack's damage and critical hit chance.

cards.name: Aerial Recovery
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self just knocked Prone or pushed
cards.effect: After the triggering displacement resolves, stand from Prone without movement cost and move 5 ft to an unoccupied space without provoking opportunity attacks. Gain 1 Momentum within the round cap. Cannot prevent falling without a legal landing.

source.originalText: Aerial Recovery: After being knocked down or back, instantly regain your footing and gain 1 Momentum.

cards.name: Dragon's Eye
cards.effect: Study it: your first polearm attack against it has advantage, and you learn one of its visible damage resistances if any. No automatic critical, secret full stat block or ability to attack through cover.

source.originalText: Dragon's Eye: Briefly gain the keen vision of a dragon, allowing you to spot weaknesses in enemy defenses and increase your critical hit range.

cards.name: Aegis Leap
cards.rangeAndTarget: Ally within 15 ft targeted by an attack
cards.effect: Before the attack roll, leap to an empty space adjacent to ally using this supplied movement. Become the target if the attack can reach you; resolve against your AC. Cannot be used if restrained or no path. Counts as your one intercept reaction.

source.originalText: Aegis Leap: Leap to an ally and intercept the next attack made against them.

cards.name: Wyrmhide
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self while above half maximum HP
cards.effect: Reduce each damage instance by 2 and gain advantage on CON saves against Bleed, Burn and Poisoned. No blanket condition immunity; effects already present persist and ordinary nonstacking reduction applies.

source.originalText: Wyrmhide: Gain +10% DR and immunity to Bleed/Burn/Poison while above 50% HP.

cards.name: Momentum Shield
cards.effect: After spending at least 1 Momentum, gain temporary HP equal to amount spent+M, maximum 10. Later expenditure replaces with the higher remaining value; no real HP restoration.

source.originalText: Momentum Shield: Spending Momentum grants temporary HP.

cards.name: Spiral Defense
cards.rangeAndTarget: Melee attacker in polearm reach that misses you while at maximum Momentum
cards.effect: Make one polearm attack. Pay Momentum after checking the maximum prerequisite. This counter grants no Momentum and cannot trigger another counter or leap. It consumes your ordinary Reaction.

source.originalText: Spiral Defense: Automatically counter melee attacks with a polearm when at max Momentum.

cards.name: Bastion Descent
cards.rangeAndTarget: Leap within 30 ft; up to 6 allies within 15 ft of landing
cards.duration: Instant; protection until start next turn
cards.effect: Land in empty space. Chosen allies gain 4d8+M temporary HP and may end Frightened or Poisoned. They gain resistance to the next damage instance before your next turn. No healing, resurrection or removal of Wounds.

source.originalText: Final Flight – Bastion Descent: Slam down between allies, cleansing effects and shielding the group.

cards.name: Guardian's Intercept
cards.rangeAndTarget: Ally within 30 ft being hit by an attack
cards.effect: Leap adjacent before damage, becoming the target of that already successful hit; halve damage to you after normal mitigation. No new roll against your AC. Requires legal path/landing. You cannot also use Aegis Leap on the same attack.

source.originalText: Guardian's Intercept: Leap to an ally's position and take the next attack targeted at them, with reduced damage to yourself.

cards.name: Draconic Ward
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self and up to 3 allies within 10 ft
cards.effect: Project a ward: chosen creatures while within 10 ft reduce damage by S, minimum 0. The reduction does not stack with Wyrmhide or another flat class reduction. No passive healing or extra Actions.

source.originalText: Draconic Ward: Channel draconic energy to create a protective aura around yourself and nearby allies, reducing incoming damage.

cards.name: Wyrmscale Defense
cards.effect: Gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing and advantage on saves against Poisoned, Frightened and Stunned. This is not immunity; existing conditions still require their ordinary removal.

source.originalText: Wyrmscale Defense: Temporarily harden your skin like dragon scales, gaining significant damage reduction and status effect resistance.

cards.name: Momentum Barrier
cards.effect: Spend K Momentum. Each gains K+S d6 temporary HP, using one shared dice roll. These HP do not stack with other shields and no unspent Momentum remains. This is not concentration.

source.originalText: Momentum Barrier: Convert your Momentum into a protective shield that absorbs damage for you and nearby allies.

cards.name: Dragon's Sanctuary
cards.rangeAndTarget: Fixed 15 ft-radius zone centered within 30 ft; up to 6 allies
cards.effect: Chosen allies inside reduce damage by 5 and have advantage against Frightened/Charmed. On start and each of your next 2 turns, Bonus Action lets one ally inside repeat one save against a present Frightened, Charmed or Poisoned effect. No automatic mass cleanse each turn.

source.originalText: Dragon's Sanctuary: Ultimate ability that creates a zone of protection, significantly reducing damage to all allies within range and cleansing negative effects.

cards.name: Drake Mark
cards.rangeAndTarget: One creature hit by your leap
cards.effect: Mark that creature; your first subsequent direct polearm hit adds S damage. A new mark replaces old. No extra damage to the triggering leap, Do Ts or copies; it is not a spell mark.

source.originalText: Drake Mark: Each leap attack marks enemies. Marked enemies take +10% damage from you.

cards.name: Elemental Spearcraft
cards.effect: Choose fire, cold or lightning. Once/own turn one polearm hit adds 1d6 chosen damage. Switching requires a new activation and full cost. Does not stack with Elemental Lance's bonus; use stronger.

source.originalText: Elemental Spearcraft: Infuse polearms with Fire, Ice, or Lightning for 3 turns (switchable).

cards.name: Air Mastery
cards.effect: Increase leap range by 10 ft, not vertical ceiling penetration or flight. After a successful leap hit, shorten one OTHER positive leap cooldown by 1 using its reset allowance. Does not combine with Wyvern's Flow on the same counter in a round.

source.originalText: Air Mastery: Gain +20% jump range and 10% reduced cooldown on leap skills.

cards.name: Momentum Tempo
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self after spending at least 3 Momentum on a technique this turn
cards.effect: Pay 3 additional Momentum now to gain one extra full Action on your next turn. Shared cap applies; it cannot grant another Action or another Momentum Tempo. Triggering technique must have been paid without this additional cost. No queued actions.

source.originalText: Momentum Tempo: After spending 3+ Momentum in a round, gain an extra action next turn.

cards.name: Drakestorm Dive
cards.rangeAndTarget: Leap up to 60 ft; up to 6 enemies within 15 ft of landing
cards.effect: Choose fire/cold/lightning. DEX save:6d8 chosen damage, half on success. On failure fire applies Burn, cold reduces Speed 10 ft until end next turn, lightning prevents Reactions until then. Land in legal empty space; no additional weapon attack.

source.originalText: Final Flight – Drakestorm Dive: Choose an element and leap into a group, triggering a large AoE blast.

cards.name: Elemental Lance
cards.effect: Choose fire/cold/lightning. Once/own turn a hit adds S d4 damage; fire adds 1 damage, cold reduces target Speed 5 ft until end next turn, lightning denies opportunity attacks until start its next turn. Nonstacking with Spearcraft; one element rider/turn.

source.originalText: Elemental Lance: Infuse your weapon with elemental energy (fire, ice, or lightning), adding additional damage and effects to your attacks.

cards.name: Drake's Agility
cards.effect: Gain+20 ft Speed and may replace 10 ft of normal movement with a leap of 10 ft horizontally/5 ft vertically. This is movement only, not another leap attack or technique. No new Action or attack is granted.

source.originalText: Drake's Agility: Channel the speed of a drake, significantly increasing your movement speed and allowing an additional leap this turn.

cards.name: Aerial Combo
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to 2 enemies adjacent to legal landings within 30 ft
cards.effect: Leap to first target, attack once, then leap up to 15 ft to second and attack once. All movement supplied by Action; two attacks maximum even with Extra Attack. Add 1d6 to each hit. Only one hit-generated Momentum per turn.

source.originalText: Aerial Combo: Perform a rapid series of attacks while airborne, building and consuming Momentum with each strike.

cards.name: Elemental Adaptation
cards.effect: Choose fire/cold/lightning: gain resistance to that type and may convert normal polearm weapon damage to it. This adds no damage and cannot combine with another resistance multiplicatively. Choice fixed for duration.

source.originalText: Elemental Adaptation: Temporarily gain resistance to a chosen element and infuse your attacks with that element.

cards.name: Drakestorm
cards.rangeAndTarget: Moving 10 ft aura; up to 3 enemies per pulse
cards.effect: Choose element. Start and on each of next 2 turns, Bonus Action pulses S d6 damage, DEX half. During duration Speed+10 ft. No free weapon attacks or Momentum from pulse damage; maximum 3 pulses.

source.originalText: Drakestorm: Ultimate ability that summons a swirling storm of elemental energy around you, dealing damage to nearby enemies and enhancing your mobility.

cards.name: Tyrant's Crash
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to 2 enemies within 5 ft of your leap landing
cards.effect: After a leap hit pay 1. Targets make WIS save; on failure Frightened and-1 AC. Save repeated at each turn end ends both. This neither stacks AC penalties nor affects enemies beyond the printed area.

source.originalText: Tyrant's Crash: Leap attack applies Fear and Sunder Armor in an AoE.

cards.name: Momentum Feeder
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self on polearm critical or hostile kill
cards.effect: Gain 2 Momentum, still within total 2-per-round gain cap. A critical kill is one trigger, not two. Do Ts, copies, allies, summons and helpless creatures cannot trigger it.

source.originalText: Momentum Feeder: Killing or critting grants +2 Momentum.

cards.name: Wyrmblood Surge
cards.effect: After spending Momentum, your next direct polearm hit adds damage equal to points spent, maximum 5. Further spending replaces rather than adds this bonus. It is flat damage and grants no resource refund.

source.originalText: Wyrmblood Surge: Each Momentum spent grants +5% damage for the next 2 turns.

cards.name: Skypiercer Stance
cards.effect: Increase leap vertical clearance allowance by 10 ft, never through solid obstacles. Once/own turn a natural 19 polearm hit critically hits; use the broadest critical range rather than stacking. It does not let you remain flying.

source.originalText: Skypiercer Stance: Gain passive +15% crit and ignore height restrictions on leaps.

cards.name: Sovereign Descent
cards.rangeAndTarget: Leap up to 60 ft; up to 6 enemies within 15 ft
cards.effect: STR save:6d8 bludgeoning, half on success. Failure knocks Prone and applies one Bleed and Burn. Failure by 10 also Stuns until end target's next turn, subject to denial cap. Ground becomes difficult terrain for 1 minute; no destruction of structural supports.

source.originalText: Final Flight – Sovereign Descent: Break the ground in a large radius, stunning enemies and applying Bleed and Burn. (1/rest)

cards.name: Tyrant's Impale
cards.duration: Instant; pin until end next turn
cards.effect: Weapon attack; hit adds S d6 piercing. A hit creature no more than one size larger makes STR save or is Restrained and Bleeding. It may use Action STR(Athletics) or DEX(Acrobatics) versus class DC to end restraint. You must stay in reach to maintain pin.

source.originalText: Tyrant's Impale: A devastating attack that can pin weaker enemies to the ground, preventing movement and causing bleeding damage.

cards.name: Draconic Dominance
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to 3 enemies within 30 ft that hear you
cards.effect: WIS save or Frightened; each repeats save at its turn end. On failure by 10 it must use up to 10 ft of its next normal movement away from you by a safe route, not a full Action or hazardous compulsory movement.

source.originalText: Draconic Dominance: Channel the terrifying presence of a dragon, causing fear in nearby enemies and potentially causing them to flee.

cards.name: Momentum Rampage
cards.effect: Once/own turn your first polearm hit adds S d6 damage. Gain+10 ft Speed but suffer-1 AC. No extra attacks, Actions, crit range or scaling from an unbounded resource count.

source.originalText: Momentum Rampage: Enter a state of draconic fury, gaining increased damage and attack speed based on your current Momentum.

cards.name: Terrain Shatter
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to 4 enemies in 10 ft radius centered within polearm reach
cards.effect: STR save: (S+1)d6 bludgeoning, half on success; failure Prone. Ground becomes difficult terrain, excluding reinforced structures and magical floors. This creates neither a pit nor free falling damage.

source.originalText: Terrain Shatter: A powerful ground strike that damages enemies in an area and creates difficult terrain.

cards.name: Wyrmking's Wrath
cards.effect: Your first leap technique each turn costs 1 less Momentum, minimum 1, and its first hit adds 1d8 damage. Once during duration convert one non-Finale Action leap to Bonus Action, paying costs; consumes your one free/Bonus Action leap allowance and grants no extra Action.

source.originalText: Wyrmking's Wrath: Ultimate ability that channels pure draconic power, greatly enhancing your leap attacks and allowing rapid successive jumps for a short duration.

warrior.protectedInterfaceOriginal: No general Weave casting; mutations and serums are the Warrior's power engine.
engine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. At Warrior level 1 choose Strength or Dexterity as your Warrior ability; this choice is permanent in this draft. S = 1/2/3/4 at Warrior levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, chosen Warrior ability modifier). Warrior technique attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + chosen modifier. Warrior technique save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + chosen modifier. Source basis: approved Player Rulebook extract and preserved class registry.

The Warrior remains three distinct stages: Base Warrior at levels 1-2, Arch Juggernaut at levels 3-9, then one Hero path at levels 10-20: Wardborn, Ironskin or Dreadspawn. Mutation trees and serums supplement those stages rather than replacing them or functioning as parallel classes.

MUTATION SLOTS. At Warrior 1 you have one mutation slot; slot II unlocks at Warrior 5, slot III at Warrior 13 and slot IV at Warrior 20. During a completed short or long rest, equip one eligible mutation in each slot. Equipped mutations are dormant until activated unless their text explicitly says otherwise. You cannot equip the same named mutation twice.

ACTIVE MUTATIONS. Before Juggernaut Mutation Efficiency, only one equipped mutation can be active at a time. Mutation Efficiency raises the ordinary simultaneous-active limit to two. Transcendent, Apex Form and other explicit features can temporarily exceed that limit. Activating a mutation beyond the current limit ends one active mutation of your choice unless an explicit exception permits otherwise.

SERUM RESERVE. After a long rest prepare two serum doses, choosing one of the six serum profiles for each dose. At Warrior 11 the reserve becomes three prepared doses; at Warrior 20 it becomes four. Used doses do not naturally refill on a short rest. A long rest refills the reserve. Serum Recycling and explicit class features can preserve or restore doses, but no effect can increase the reserve above its current capacity.

SERUM INJECTION. Unless another feature says otherwise, injecting a prepared serum is a Bonus Action, consumes one prepared dose, activates one equipped mutation for 3 rounds and applies that dose's serum-profile benefits and side effect for the same 3 rounds. Reinjecting the same active mutation refreshes its duration rather than stacking it. Serum-profile numeric bonuses from two doses of the same profile never stack.

STRAIN. Begin after a long rest at 0 Strain; maximum Strain is 3. A normal serum injection or Mutagen Injection adds 1 Strain, Mutation Surge adds 1, and Serum Cocktail or Mutation Overload adds 2 unless modified. At Strain 2 your Speed is reduced by 5 feet. At Strain 3 you also take -1 AC and -1 on saving throws and cannot voluntarily activate another serum, Cocktail, Overclock or Surge until Strain is reduced. A completed short rest reduces Strain by 1; a long rest resets it to 0. Strain cannot exceed 3.

Mutation Adaptation and Serum Tolerance modify Strain and serum-profile side effects only as their cards state. A negative serum-profile side effect and Strain penalty are separate; preventing one does not automatically prevent the other.

BRUTALITY PROGRESS. Begin each real encounter with Brutality Progress 0 and BT 0. Add actual damage you personally deal to meaningful hostile creatures to Brutality Progress, but a single damage event contributes no more than one-quarter of your maximum HP. Crossing cumulative thresholds equal to 25%, 50% and 75% of your maximum HP grants 1 BT each, subject to the BT cap. Crossing 100% triggers Transcendent as described below but does not create a fourth stored BT unless Stack Overflow or another feature raises the cap.

TAKING DAMAGE AND BT. Once per round when one source deals you actual damage after mitigation equal to or greater than PB + M, gain 1 BT. This direct gain does not increase Brutality Progress. Normal threshold and damage-taken generation together can grant at most 2 BT per round. Explicit card gains such as Overpressure Response or Backlash Engine ignore that generation ceiling but never exceed the current BT cap.

BT CAP AND RESET. Default BT cap is 3. Stack Overflow raises it to 4. BT is not automatically spent; only features explicitly saying spend reduce it. Encounter end resets BT and Brutality Progress to 0. BT cannot be generated from friendly attacks, summoned sacrificial creatures, unattended objects, staged sparring or enemies that do not meaningfully threaten the party.

BRUTALITY STATES. At BT 1 you are Awakened; at BT 2 Primed; at BT 3 Unleashed. At Warrior 12+, reaching BT 4 or crossing 100% Brutality Progress may trigger the same once-per-encounter Transcendent pulse, even if your stored cap remains 3; it is never an indefinitely active state. State benefits are defined as operational extra Cards and vanish immediately if spending BT drops you below their thresholds.

HARD CONTROL GUARD. A creature can suffer at most one Warrior-caused effect that fully denies its normal turn, such as Stunned, Paralyzed or an equivalent full-turn denial, from your Warrior features per encounter. After the first succeeds, later Warrior effects from you that would fully deny that creature's turn instead remove its Reaction and reduce its Speed to 0 until the end of its next turn after the required save fails.

ADDITIONAL ACTION GUARD. All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot generate another Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Free attacks granted by Warrior features are explicitly bounded and never recursively grant additional free attacks.

RECHARGE GUARD. A named ability may receive at most one positive-counter reset or shortening per round. Only an ability with a positive recharge counter can be reset. Recharge never restores a spent short-rest or long-rest use unless the feature explicitly says it restores that use.

HEALING AND REGENERATION. Warrior healing cannot exceed maximum HP, restore the dead or remove Wounds unless a card explicitly says otherwise. Regeneration and repeated healing effects operate only during real encounters unless their card explicitly permits downtime healing. No corpse, summoned creature, trivial enemy or friendly target can be used to create infinite healing, serum doses or BT.

IMMUNITY AND RESISTANCE. Warrior resistance does not stack with resistance to the same damage type; apply one resistance. Immunity supersedes resistance but multiple immunities provide no additional benefit. If a feature grants several immunities temporarily, each is still only one immunity to that specific type or condition.

MUTATION TIERS. Basic mutations require Warrior 1. Advanced mutations require Warrior 6. Apex mutations require Warrior 15. You may equip only mutations whose actual Warrior class-level gate and other prerequisites you meet. NEW explicit scope reconciliation (FEAT327-ACQ-02): across your single set of unlocked mutation slots, you may equip at most two Advanced mutations from each actual mutation tree and at most one Apex mutation in total across all trees. Basic mutations have no additional tier-count ceiling beyond the remaining unlocked slots. Count every equipped mutation, including a dormant one, toward its relevant equipment ceilings; use its actual source-defined tree and tier. These are equipped-loadout ceilings, not per-tree slot grants, limits on the number of feat identities acquired, or separate active-only tier ceilings. The completed-rest equipping procedure and prohibition on duplicate named mutations remain unchanged. Mutation Efficiency changes only the ordinary global simultaneous-active limit. Transcendent and Apex Form activate only the existing legally equipped loadout and do not waive equipment ceilings, level/prerequisite gates or duplicate restrictions. Apex Form's permanent slot IV is the single Warrior-20 slot unlock, not an additional slot each time the form activates. After a temporary activation exception ends, apply its exact ending procedure and the then-applicable active-mutation limit without refreshing durations or granting an unequipped mutation.

MUTATION FEATS. Mutation feats are not free mutation selections. They become eligible choices at an ASI/feat opportunity or other campaign feat grant once their listed level and mutation prerequisite are met. They do not consume mutation slots unless their own text says otherwise.

HERO MUTATION TREES. Bulwark Mutation Tree, Gore Mutation Tree and Aberrant Mutation Tree are Hero cards that unlock their associated Hero-specific mutation extra Cards. Those mutations still occupy normal mutation slots and obey active-mutation, serum and Strain rules.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Warrior 1 automatically gains Mutation Slot I and the BT tracker, then chooses 4 Base cards with at least 2 Active. Warrior 2 automatically gains Mutagen Injection, then chooses 2 additional Base cards. Warrior 3 enters Juggernaut and chooses 2 Arch cards with at least 1 Active. Warrior levels 4-9 each grant one eligible unselected Base or Arch choice. Source progression automatic features remain separate and never consume these choices.

At Warrior 10 choose Wardborn, Ironskin or Dreadspawn and choose 2 Hero cards from that path. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base or Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. The chosen Hero Final Form is automatic at Warrior 20 and cannot be selected early. ASI/feat grants remain separate.

SOURCE PROGRESSION RECONCILIATION. Book progression grants Mutation Slot II at 5, Bone Hardened at 6, Serum Overclock at 9, Mutation Slot III at 13, Brutal Adaptation at 15, Reflexive Mutation at 17 and Apex Form at 20 automatically. Registry-only Fighting Style, Second Wind, Action Surge, Extra Attack and draft level features are preserved in excluded Registry Alternatives and original source evidence. They are not acquired or stacked onto this playtest schedule.

All class gates use Warrior class level, not total character level. Proficiency bonus follows the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. No other class level unlocks Warrior mutation tiers, serum capacity, Juggernaut, Hero paths, Apex mutations or Final Forms.

Finite recovery completion: Mutation Recovery Reserve=3 L+M HP after a long rest. Bloodthick Node, Rapid Coagulation, Regenerative Mutation, Hemophage Core and their healing enhancements draw from this shared reserve, 1 point per actual HP healed. No short-rest refill; no gauge, critical hit, free activation or form change replenishes it. Other explicitly limited-use/dose healing retains its own printed limit. This new test reserve prevents indefinite regenerative healing from free mutation activations.
workedExample: Warrior 6 example: chosen ability Strength 18 gives M=4; assume PB=3, S=2, maximum HP 60, two mutation slots and Mutation Efficiency. The Warrior equips Ironhide Graft and Shock Muscle Weave, prepares Overdrive and Stonecore, begins a real encounter at BT 0, Brutality Progress 0 and Strain 0.

Turn 1: Bonus Action Serum Injection consumes the Overdrive dose, activates Ironhide Graft for 3 rounds and adds Strain 0→1. Overdrive grants +2 Strength and +10 feet Speed; its side effect gives -1 AC. Ironhide grants its own active mutation defenses. The Warrior then deals 18 actual damage; Brutality Progress becomes 18, crossing the 15-point 25% threshold and granting BT 0→1.

Enemy round: one attack deals 11 actual damage after mitigation. PB+M is 7, so the damage-taken rule grants BT 1→2, subject to the round generation cap. At BT 2 the Warrior is Primed. The damage itself does not add to Brutality Progress.

Turn 2: Serum Injection consumes Stonecore, activates Shock Muscle Weave alongside Ironhide because Mutation Efficiency permits two active mutations, and adds Strain 1→2. Stonecore grants +2 AC and knockback immunity but -10 feet Speed. Strain 2 separately applies -5 feet Speed. The Warrior deals 20 damage, Brutality Progress 18→38, crossing the 30-point 50% threshold; BT is already 2 so it becomes 3.

Turn 3: with BT 3 the Warrior is Unleashed and uses Brutality Unleashed, spending all 3 BT. BT 3→0. Enemies in the burst make the printed Strength save and take the area damage. Spending BT immediately ends Awakened, Primed and Unleashed state benefits, but active mutations and serum durations continue independently.

Turn 4: the Warrior uses Mutation Surge on Ironhide, adding 1 Strain. Strain 2→3, so the Strain 3 AC/save penalty applies after the activation. Until Strain falls below 3, another voluntary Serum Injection, Cocktail, Overclock or Surge is illegal. A later completed short rest reduces Strain 3→2 but does not refill either consumed serum dose.
balanceQuestions: Do BT accumulation, the three stored states and the 100%-progress Transcendent pulse create a meaningful escalating fight rhythm without making high-damage builds enter Unleashed or Transcendent too early?
Are mutation slots, active-mutation concurrency, serum dose scarcity and Strain restrictive enough to make preparation meaningful without leaving Warrior powerless after only one or two encounters?

Do Wardborn mitigation, Ironskin regeneration/adaptation and Dreadspawn control/damage remain comparable after all mutation-tree, Apex and serum interactions are active, especially around Extra Attack and free-attack sources?

cards.name: Mutation Adaptation
cards.effect: Mutation Adaptation. Ignore the Strain-2 Speed penalty. The first time in each encounter that activating a mutation or serum would add Strain, reduce that Strain gain by 1, minimum 0. This reduction cannot reduce Serum Cocktail or Mutation Overload below 1 Strain and cannot reduce existing Strain.

source.originalText: Mutation Adaptation: Your body has been conditioned to accept mutations with reduced side effects.

cards.name: Serum Tolerance
cards.effect: Serum Tolerance. Negative side effects printed on serum profiles do not affect you. Strain generation and Strain penalties still apply normally. This does not suppress drawbacks printed on mutation cards, Hero transformations or Mutation Overload.

source.originalText: Serum Tolerance: You can consume serums without the normal toxicity effects that would affect others.

cards.name: Combat Instinct
cards.effect: Combat Instinct. Gain +1 on initiative rolls. You cannot be Surprised while conscious unless the opposing creature's Stealth check exceeds your passive Perception by 5 or more. This does not grant extra Actions or movement before combat.

source.originalText: Combat Instinct: +5% initiative and +10% resistance to being surprised.

cards.name: Physical Conditioning
cards.effect: Physical Conditioning. Increase carrying, pushing, dragging and lifting capacity by 25%. You have advantage on Constitution checks and saving throws made specifically against forced marching, sustained physical exertion, suffocation from exertion or environmental fatigue.

source.originalText: Physical Conditioning: +10% carrying capacity and advantage on physical endurance checks.

cards.name: Brutality Sense
cards.rangeAndTarget: Hostile creatures you can perceive within 60 feet
cards.effect: Brutality Sense. You know when a visible hostile creature is at or below one-quarter of its maximum HP; it is Vulnerable for your Warrior features that specifically reference a marked vulnerable target. This does not reveal its exact HP or hidden resistances.

source.originalText: Brutality Sense: You can sense when an opponent is below 25% health, marking them as vulnerable.

cards.name: Serum Injection
cards.frequency: At will while legal doses remain
cards.effect: Serum Injection. Choose one equipped mutation and one prepared serum dose. Consume the dose, activate that mutation for 3 rounds and apply the serum profile for 3 rounds. Observe active-mutation limits, Strain legality and nonstacking same-profile bonuses.

source.originalText: Serum Injection: Activate a prepared mutation serum as a bonus action, triggering its effects for 3 rounds.

cards.name: Brutal Strike
cards.rangeAndTarget: One creature within your weapon reach
cards.duration: Instantaneous; Stagger until end of target's next turn
cards.effect: Brutal Strike. Make one melee weapon attack using its normal ability. On hit add S d6 damage of the weapon's type. The target makes a Constitution save; on failure it is Staggered, taking -1 on attack rolls and -5 feet Speed until the end of its next turn. This is not a full-turn denial.

source.originalText: Brutal Strike: A powerful attack that deals additional damage based on your Strength and has a chance to stagger the target.

cards.name: Mutation Surge
cards.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
cards.effect: Mutation Surge. Enhance one active mutation. If it grants AC, DR, attack, save or flat damage, increase one such bonus by 1; if it grants movement or reach, increase it by 5 feet; if it deals mutation damage, add 1d4 to one damage event. A mutation with none of those numeric effects instead grants S temporary HP. The enhancement never changes immunity, target count or duration.

source.originalText: Mutation Surge: Temporarily enhance an active mutation, increasing its effects for 1 round but adding strain to your body.

cards.name: Intimidating Presence
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to 3 enemies of your choice within 15 feet that can see or hear you
cards.effect: Intimidating Presence. Each target makes a Wisdom save. On failure it is Frightened of you until the end of its next turn, then repeats the save. A second failure extends the fear one final round. A creature that succeeds becomes immune to this use. This never forces surrender; NPC surrender remains a Director decision.

source.originalText: Intimidating Presence: Use your mutated appearance to frighten enemies, potentially causing them to flee or surrender.

cards.name: Survival Instinct
cards.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
cards.effect: Survival Instinct. Gain +2 on Perception checks, +2 on Dexterity saving throws and one additional Reaction usable only for Dodge-like defensive reactions, opportunity-free movement granted by a feature, or Deflect-style mitigation. It cannot make an attack or trigger another additional Reaction.

source.originalText: Survival Instinct: Enter a heightened state of awareness, gaining bonuses to perception and reaction time for a short duration.

cards.name: Mutation Efficiency
cards.effect: Mutation Efficiency. You may maintain up to two equipped mutations active simultaneously instead of one. Activating a third mutation while two are already active requires choosing one active mutation to become dormant unless another explicit feature temporarily raises this limit. Mutation slots, serum costs, Strain and mutation durations remain unchanged.

source.originalText: Mutation Efficiency: May have 2 active mutations at once (Lv 3)

cards.name: Brutal Fortitude
cards.effect: Brutal Fortitude. Reduce damage you take by 1 for each current BT, to a maximum DR 3 from this feature. Stack Overflow can raise your BT cap to 4 but does not raise Brutal Fortitude above DR 3. Losing or spending BT immediately lowers this DR.

source.originalText: Brutal Fortitude: Gain +1 DR for each BT stack (max +3)

cards.name: Overpressure Response
cards.duration: 3 rounds or its shorter printed duration
cards.effect: Overpressure Response. When you take a critical hit, choose one equipped dormant non-Apex mutation and activate it without consuming a serum dose or gaining Strain. This activation must respect your normal simultaneous-active-mutation limit; if necessary, make another active mutation dormant. It grants no serum-profile benefit and cannot activate a mutation whose prerequisite you do not meet.

source.originalText: Overpressure Response: Once per round, when struck by a critical hit, gain 1 free mutation activation

cards.name: Crushing Advance
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self; 20-foot straight movement path and creatures crossed or approached within 5 feet
cards.effect: Crushing Advance. Move up to 20 feet in a straight line without provoking opportunity attacks. Each enemy no more than one size larger whose space or reach-line you pass through or adjacent to makes a Strength save. On failure it takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage, is pushed to the nearest legal space outside your path and falls Prone. On success it takes half damage and is neither pushed nor Prone. A creature is affected once per use.

source.originalText: Crushing Advance: Once per long rest, move in a straight line up to 20 ft, knocking aside all enemies (STR save or fall prone, take 2d6)

cards.name: Pain Conversion
cards.duration: Until end of your next regular turn
cards.effect: Pain Conversion. After one damage event deals actual damage to you, gain a temporary Power bonus equal to floor(actual damage/10), minimum 1 and maximum 3. Until the end of your next regular turn, add that bonus to one Strength-based weapon damage roll or Strength check. A later trigger refreshes the duration and replaces the previous bonus rather than stacking.

source.originalText: Pain Conversion: Convert 10% of damage taken into temporary Strength bonus.

cards.name: Adaptive Tissue
cards.duration: Until completion of a short or long rest
cards.frequency: One remembered damage type at a time
cards.effect: Adaptive Tissue. When a critical hit deals acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, poison, psychic, radiant or thunder damage to you, gain resistance to one such damage type dealt by that hit until you complete a short or long rest. Gaining a new Adaptive Tissue resistance replaces the previous one. Immunity and duplicate resistance do not stack.

source.originalText: Adaptive Tissue: Gain resistance to the last damage type that critically hit you until your next rest.

cards.name: Brutality Momentum
cards.effect: Brutality Momentum. When you personally reduce a creature marked Vulnerable by Brutality Sense to 0 HP with a melee attack, set Brutal Strike's positive round-recharge counter to 0 if it has not already been reset or shortened this round. This restores no Action and cannot refresh a per-rest use. Trivial, summoned or friendly creatures cannot trigger it.

source.originalText: Brutality Momentum: Killing a marked vulnerable target instantly readies your next Brutal Strike.

cards.name: Mutation Overload
cards.duration: 2 rounds; backlash until end of following turn
cards.effect: Mutation Overload. For 2 rounds, enhance each currently active mutation once: an AC, DR, attack, save or flat-damage bonus increases by 1; a movement or reach bonus increases by 5 feet; or one mutation damage/healing roll gains +1d4. Immunities, target counts, resource generation and action grants cannot be increased. When Overload ends, you suffer -1 on attack rolls and saving throws and -5 feet Speed until the end of your next regular turn. This activation is illegal if +2 Strain would exceed the Strain cap.

source.originalText: Mutation Overload: Push your mutations beyond safe limits, gaining significantly enhanced effects for 2 rounds followed by exhaustion.

cards.name: Serum Cocktail
cards.cost: Consume 2 different prepared serum doses; +2 Strain
cards.effect: Serum Cocktail. Choose two different prepared serum profiles, consume both doses and apply both profiles to yourself for 3 rounds while activating one eligible equipped mutation. Same-stat bonuses use only the stronger value. Both profile side effects apply unless Serum Tolerance suppresses them. This activates only one mutation and therefore differs from Serum Overclock. It is illegal if the resulting Strain would exceed 3.

source.originalText: Serum Cocktail: Combine two different serums for a hybrid effect, though with increased strain on your body.

cards.name: Brutality Unleashed
cards.cost: Spend all 3 BT; requires Unleashed state
cards.rangeAndTarget: Enemies of your choice within 15 feet
cards.frequency: At will when requirement is met
cards.effect: Brutality Unleashed. Spend all 3 BT. Each chosen enemy within 15 feet makes a Strength save, taking (S+1)d8 + M bludgeoning damage and being pushed 10 feet on failure, or half damage with no push on success. Spending the BT immediately ends Awakened, Primed and Unleashed state benefits. This is one area attack and cannot generate BT or Brutality Progress from its own damage.

source.originalText: Brutality Unleashed: Once your Brutality Threshold is crossed, unleash a devastating area attack that damages all enemies within range.

cards.name: Survival Adaptation
cards.effect: Survival Adaptation. Choose one hazard when activated: extreme heat, extreme cold, poisonous atmosphere, high altitude/low oxygen, corrosive environment or difficult natural terrain. For 3 rounds you ignore ordinary environmental penalties from that hazard; if it deals acid, cold, fire or poison damage, you instead gain resistance to that one damage type. This grants no immunity and does not protect allies.

source.originalText: Survival Adaptation: Rapidly adapt your body to environmental hazards, gaining temporary resistance to environmental effects.

cards.name: Intimidating Transformation
cards.rangeAndTarget: Up to 3 enemies of your choice within 20 feet that can see you
cards.effect: Intimidating Transformation. Each target makes a Wisdom save. On failure it is Frightened of you until the end of its next turn and then repeats the save. On a failure by 10 or more, it would instead be Stunned until the end of its next turn, subject to the Warrior hard-control guard. A target succeeding on the initial save is immune to this use. The transformation does not force surrender or belief changes.

source.originalText: Intimidating Transformation: Undergo a particularly terrifying mutation that can cause enemies to become frightened or even paralyzed with fear.

cards.name: Guardian Tissue
cards.effect: Guardian Tissue. When an adjacent ally would take damage, reduce that ally's incoming damage by one-third rounded down. You take the prevented amount as damage of the same type. This transferred damage cannot be redirected again and cannot trigger another Guardian Tissue. Transferred damage cannot be reduced again, redirected again or generate BT.

source.originalText: Guardian Tissue: When an adjacent ally would take damage, you can absorb 30% of it as a reaction.

cards.name: Protective Mutations
cards.rangeAndTarget: Allies within 5 feet while you have at least one active mutation
cards.effect: Protective Mutations. While at least one mutation is active, each ally other than you within 5 feet reduces the first damage it takes each round by S, minimum 0. Multiple Protective Mutations do not stack. The protection ends immediately when the ally leaves the aura or you have no active mutation.

source.originalText: Protective Mutations: Your mutations generate a 5-foot aura that grants allies +10% damage resistance.

cards.name: Serum Sharing
cards.rangeAndTarget: One willing living ally you touch
cards.frequency: At most once per ally per short rest
cards.effect: Serum Sharing. Inject one willing ally with a diluted prepared serum. The ally receives half of each positive numeric benefit of that serum profile, rounded down with minimum 1, for 3 rounds; nonnumeric immunities become advantage on the relevant save instead. The serum activates no mutation in the ally. The ally gains 1 Strain for this pilot and suffers the profile's printed side effect. Your Serum Tolerance does not protect the ally.

source.originalText: Serum Sharing: You can safely inject allies with diluted versions of your serums, granting them 50% of the benefits.

cards.name: Controlled Transformation
cards.effect: Controlled Transformation. You can suppress obvious cosmetic signs of dormant mutations and reduce visible manifestations of active mutations enough to pass as merely scarred or unusually built while fully clothed. You gain advantage on checks to conceal your Warrior mutations from casual visual inspection. This never suppresses mechanical mutation effects, defeats magical detection or conceals transformations whose cards explicitly make you Large, monstrous or otherwise impossible to hide.

source.originalText: Controlled Transformation: Your mutations appear less monstrous and can be partially concealed when necessary.

cards.name: Aegis Incarnate
cards.effect: Final Form – Aegis Incarnate. For 3 rounds you cannot be forcibly moved or knocked Prone. Whenever an ally within 15 feet takes damage, automatically redirect half that damage rounded down to yourself after the ally's resistance but before its temporary HP; the ally takes the remainder. Redirected damage keeps its type, cannot be reduced again or generate BT, and cannot be redirected again. If taking the redirected damage would kill you outright, the redirection still occurs. This grants no extra Reaction requirement and does not stack with Guardian Tissue on the same damage event.

source.originalText: Final Form – Aegis Incarnate: Transform into a living shield for 3 rounds, becoming immovable and redirecting 50% of all damage dealt to allies within 15 feet to yourself.

cards.name: Bulwark Mutation Tree
cards.effect: Bulwark Mutation Tree. Unlock the Wardborn-specific mutations Spinal Plating, Adrenal Overwatch and Living Cover as eligible mutation choices. They occupy normal mutation slots, require serum activation unless their card says otherwise, and obey all active-mutation, tier and Strain rules. Selecting this card does not automatically equip or activate any of them.

source.originalText: Bulwark Mutation Tree: Unlocks mutations like:

cards.name: Mutated Guard
cards.rangeAndTarget: One ally within 10 feet when your turn ends
cards.duration: Until start of your next regular turn
cards.effect: Mutated Guard. If you end your turn within 10 feet of at least one ally, choose one such ally. Until the start of your next regular turn it gains +1 on saving throws and reduces the first damage it takes by 1. This benefit does not stack with another Mutated Guard.

source.originalText: Mutated Guard: If you end your turn within 2 tiles of an ally, grant them +1 Save and DR

cards.name: Guardian Pulse
cards.rangeAndTarget: One adjacent ally and triggering attacker
cards.effect: Guardian Pulse. Trigger when an adjacent ally is targeted by an attack. You become the target instead; resolve the original attack roll against your AC and defenses. After that attack fully resolves, if the attacker is within your melee reach, make one melee weapon attack against it. This counterattack is a free attack, cannot grant another free attack or Action, and occurs whether the redirected attack hit or missed.

source.originalText: Guardian Pulse: 1/rest, redirect an attack from an adjacent ally to yourself and immediately counterstrike

cards.name: Warding Mutation
cards.rangeAndTarget: Self; protects one ally within 10 feet at a time
cards.effect: Warding Mutation. Grow temporary protective plates for 3 rounds. At the start of each of your turns choose one ally within 10 feet. Until the start of your next turn, the first time that ally takes damage reduce it by S+M, minimum 0. The prevented damage is simply negated rather than transferred.
